title: Count Pairs That Form a Complete Day II
statement: Every entry of `hours` is a length of time in hours. Count the index pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` whose total `hours[i] + hours[j]` is a whole number of days, meaning it is divisible by 24 (24, 48, 72 and so on), and return that count.
notes:
## Intuition

Testing every pair is O(n²), far too slow for 5·10^5 values. Only the remainder modulo 24 decides whether two hours add up to whole days: `a + b` is a multiple of 24 exactly when `b % 24` equals `(24 - a % 24) % 24`. So while scanning left to right, each hour can be paired with all earlier hours at once by looking up how many of them had the complementary remainder.

## Approach

1. Keep `seen`, a map from a remainder (0 to 23) to how many earlier hours had it, and a running total `pairs`.
2. For each `hour`, compute `remainder = hour % 24` and the remainder it needs from a partner, `needed = (24 - remainder) % 24`.
3. Every earlier hour with remainder `needed` forms a valid pair with this one, so add `seen.get(needed)` to `pairs`.
4. Only then record the current hour by incrementing the count of `remainder`.
5. Return `pairs`.

## Example 1, step by step

`hours = [12, 12, 30, 24, 24]`.

- `12`: remainder 12 needs 12; none seen yet. `seen = {12: 1}`.
- `12`: needs 12, one is seen, so `pairs = 1`. `seen = {12: 2}`.
- `30`: remainder 6 needs 18; none. `seen` gains `6: 1`.
- `24`: remainder 0 needs 0; none. `seen` gains `0: 1`.
- `24`: needs 0, one is seen, so `pairs = 2`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one constant-time lookup and update per hour.
- Space: O(1): the map never holds more than 24 remainders.

## Pitfalls

- The partner of remainder 0 is 0, not 24; `(24 - remainder) % 24` handles both 0 and the rest.
- Look up before inserting: inserting first would pair an hour with itself whenever its remainder is 0 or 12.
- The count can reach about 1.25·10^11, beyond 32-bit integers; in Java or C keep it in a 64-bit `long`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | how many earlier hours had each remainder modulo 24 |
| `pairs` | number of whole-day pairs found so far |
| `hour` | the current value, the later index of its pairs |
| `remainder` | `hour % 24` |
| `needed` | the remainder an earlier hour must have to complete a day |

narration.2: seen counts the earlier hours by their remainder modulo 24.
narration.3: No pair has been found before the scan starts.
narration.5: Treat each hour as the second index j of its pairs.
narration.6: Only the remainder modulo 24 matters for whole days.
narration.7: A partner must bring the remainder up to a multiple of 24; % 24 maps 24 back to 0.
narration.8: Every earlier hour with that remainder makes a valid pair with this one.
narration.9: Record this hour so later hours can pair with it.
narration.11: Every pair (i, j) was counted once, when j was reached.
